description: Live-database retrieval golden set (task 174). Unlike tests/retrieval_golden.json, which scores a seeded hermetic fixture in CI, this file is scored against the memhub project database of the repository it is run in (this repo's own `.memhub/project.sqlite`, about 1,000 candidate rows including facts, decisions, tasks, ingested doc chunks and architecture sections). It is NOT run in CI: an A/B comparison is two back-to-back local runs of `memhub eval retrieval --golden tests/retrieval_golden_live.json --k 5 --json` on the same database, one on the old binary or settings and one on the new, then `memhub eval compare old.json new.json`. Matchers are case-insensitive substring checks against the hit's title and body. A `match` query passes when any top-K hit satisfies the primary answer or an `also_accept` entry; every match query's `notes` name the row that answers it, led by the primary answer: a doc chunk by its document (repo-relative path, or the document's title when the document is not in this repository) and section heading, any other row by type and id. A `kind: empty` probe asks about a topic no row covers and passes when no hit clears the relevance floor (low-confidence fallback hits are tolerated). Id prefixes: `seed-NN` real agent recall queries taken verbatim from this repo's session history (`seed-01` to `seed-34` from MCP recall calls, NN being the position in the original list, seed 13 omitted because no row stores an Orch plan; `seed-35` to `seed-58`, added 2026-10-11 by task 197, from CLI `memhub recall` calls and later sessions, `seed-48` being an empty probe); `kw-` keyword bags; `semantic-` natural-language paraphrases; `two-` two-part questions (every row answering either part is accepted); `vm-` vocabulary-mismatch queries written the way an agent would ask without knowing the stored wording, sharing no whole word of four or more letters with the title of any row named in their notes; `doc-` queries answered by an ingested doc chunk (pinned with a body needle unique to that chunk); `arch-` queries answered by a section of the architecture narrative; `empty-` and `near-` empty probes (`near-` ones are adjacent to topics memhub does cover). Fact, decision, task and architecture-section ids in `notes` refer to this repo's own database as of 2026-10-10 (2026-10-11 for `seed-35` to `seed-58`) (doc chunks are named by document and heading because chunk ids change on every re-ingest); the matchers, not the ids, decide pass or fail, so the set survives id shifts but a row edit or removal can invalidate a query. Numbers from this set are not comparable to the hermetic baseline (memhub fact retrieval.live-eval-not-comparable) and many queries are expected to fail under current settings: that headroom is the point. Every query's two `variants` were rewritten on 2026-10-11 (task 197) by writers that saw only the query text, with no repository access and no answers: a keyword form (a question form for queries that are already keyword bags) plus a sentence worded like the start of an answer that leaves the unknown part generic. About one query in six of each id prefix (sorted by id, every 6th starting at the 4th) is held out in tests/retrieval_golden_holdout.json; see that file for how to use it.
